title: Adaptive burst escrow and utilization rollup adaptor
author: Anika Rao
release_notes: Introduce adaptive burst escrow to smooth tenant microbursts and add a nightly utilization rollup to improve multi-window reporting accuracy. No API changes. Rollout gated behind feature flag and gradual canary.
description:
Motivation: Dedicated fleets experience frequent microbursts from noisy tenants that trigger aggressive autoscaler churn. This PR implements an adaptive burst escrow plus a daily utilization rollup adaptor to 1) attenuate transient burst pressure without blocking legitimate sustained load and 2) provide more stable utilization inputs for long-window quota and billing reports. Context: follows ENG-2251 (burst stability work) and ties into SUP-7812 incident followup.

What this PR does (high level):
- Adaptive burst escrow: introduces a short-lived escrow ledger that temporarily absorbs a bounded fraction of incoming concurrency when a tenant exceeds its committed throughput for <= T_escrow seconds. Escrow decays exponentially and returns credits when headroom stabilizes.
- Proportional throttle adaptor: when escrow is exhausted, apply a proportional soft-throttle rather than hard rejection to preserve graceful degradation.
- Utilization rollup adaptor: nightly job that ingests per-minute samples and computes 1h/6h/24h folded percentiles, smoothing out sampling jitter from autoscaler windows. These rollups feed billing and long-window autoscaler signals.
- Config & feature flagging: new config under dedicated.autoscaler.escrow with tunables: max_fraction, decay_tau_s, min_hold_s; rollout controlled by feature flag "escrow_v2".

Design notes and tradeoffs:
- Escrow is intentionally conservative: default max_fraction=0.15 to avoid starving other tenants. Longer decay tau reduces oscillation but can delay reclaim. We opted for exponential decay to be robust under sporadic bursts.
- Rollup job computes fold-aware percentiles to avoid bias from heavy sampling in warm pools. It is eventual-consistent for reporting and does not affect per-request routing.

Compatibility and migration:
- No wire/API changes. All changes confined to autoscaler/allocator runtime and a new metrics worker.
- Rollout plan: enable flag in a small canary region (eu-west-1) for dedicated fleets with low interference, monitor latency & 95th token cost for 48h, then expand.

Checklist: 
- [x] Unit tests for escrow ledger arithmetic and decay logic
- [x] Integration tests with autoscaler simulation harness (short bursts + sustained load)
- [x] Metrics emitted for escrow usage, throttle_rate, rollup_computed{window} 
- [x] Feature flag gating + default off in prod
- [x] Docs draft for ops runbook and tuning knobs

Related links: Linear ENG-2251, Design doc: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-2251/escrow-and-rollup-design, Ops playbook PR: docs/ops/escrow-tuning.md

Files changed (high level):
- autoscaler/escrow/ledger.go - new escrow accounting and unit tests
- autoscaler/handler/admission.go - integrate escrow checks and soft-throttle path
- autoscaler/config/escrow.yaml - default tunables and docs comments
- telemetry/rollup/worker.go - nightly rollup computation and publishing
- telemetry/rollup/fold_percentile_test.go - tests for accuracy on synthetic traces
- docs/ops/escrow-tuning.md - operator runbook and suggested thresholds
- ci/integration/autoscaler_sim_test.yaml - new sim scenarios

Notes on code: ledger.go contains a compact ring buffer for recent overage samples, plus an adaptive estimator to scale max_fraction for tenants with stable historical peaks. The soft-throttle path returns a Retry-After proportional reduction header to clients when applicable. Rollup worker uses reservoir subsampling to cap memory for high-cardinality fleets.

Diego Martinez: Please add a small safety-net that disables escrow when cluster free_capacity_percent < 8% — otherwise warm pools could be starved.
Anika Rao: Added a guard in admission.go to bypass escrow when cluster_free_pct < config.min_cluster_free_pct (default 7.5). Commented rationale.
Priya Singh: Tests look good; can you add a histogram for escrow_hold_time to check for pathological holding?
Anika Rao: Added histogram and an alert query in docs/ops for >95th percentile hold_time > 30s.
Ethan Park: Rollup algorithm looks sound; mention cost of nightly job in docs and add a rate limiter for very large fleets.
Anika Rao: Implemented reservoir subsampling with a 100k cap and defensive rate limiter.
Diego Martinez: Approved and queued for canary.
Priya Singh: Approved after minor doc tweaks.
